sections.overview: Lethrinus atlanticus, the Atlantic emperor, is a marine fish in the emperor family Lethrinidae.
sections.identification: It has an olive-brown or pinkish body, fine cheek reticulations and a pointed snout; maximum length is about 50 centimetres.
sections.habitat: It inhabits shallow coastal waters of the eastern central Atlantic, from Senegal to Gabon and nearby islands, generally to about 50 metres.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on invertebrates living on the seabed.
sections.behavior: FishBase describes it as non-migratory; species-specific behavioural observations are limited.
sections.reproduction: FishBase reports maturity near 23 centimetres, but the sources consulted give little detail on spawning.
sections.ecology: It shares its genus with the Indian Ocean snubnose emperor, Lethrinus borbonicus, but occupies the eastern Atlantic; it has a pointed snout and conical teeth, unlike that species.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment dated 2013 classified it as Least Concern.
